parts.problem_md:
![Geometric diagram shows parallel lines AB and DE with intersecting triangle BCF. Angles marked are 39° at B and 63° at F. Angle x is within triangle.](assets/001-geometric-diagram-shows-parallel-lines-ab-and-de.png)

$ABC$ is parallel to $DEFG$
$BC=BF$ 
Angle $ABE=39^{\circ}$
Angle $CFG=63^{\circ}$

Work out the size of angle $x$. 
Give a reason for each stage in your working.
parts.solution_md:
> **[exam-tip]**
> When asked to find a missing angle you will commonly need to work out other missing angles first.
> 
> Write any calculated missing angles on the diagram provided making sure you write your method and reasons as you go.
> 
> Diagrams with parallel lines will often require you to use alternate, corresponding  and co-interior angle facts.

> *As lines **ABC** and **DEFG** are parallel, angles **BCF** and **CFG** are alternate angles and are therefore equal*

$BCF=CFG=63^{\circ}$

*because alternate angles are equal*

**[M1]**

> *Calculate angle **BFC** using the fact that base angles in an isosceles triangle are equal*

$BFC=BCF=63^{^{\circ}}$

*because base angles in an isosceles triangle are equal*

> *Calculate angle **CBF** using the fact that angles in a triangle add up to 180*<sup>*o*</sup>

`table row cell 180 minus open parentheses 63 plus 63 close parentheses end cell equals cell 180 minus 126 end cell row blank equals cell 54 to the power of degree space end exponent end cell end table`

*because interior angles of a triangle add up to 180°*

**[M1]**

> *Calculate angle *$x$* using the fact that adjacent angles on a straight line add up to 180*<sup>*o*</sup>

`table row cell 180 minus open parentheses 39 plus 54 close parentheses end cell equals cell 180 minus 93 end cell row blank equals cell 87 degree end cell end table`

*because adjacent angles on a straight line add up to 180°*

**[M1 A1 A1]**

**Final answer:** **87**<sup>**o **</sup>

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **M1**: Awarded for calculating either angle *BEF*=39<sup>o</sup> or angle *BCF*=63<sup>o</sup>
> 
> **M1**: Awarded for showing correct method for calculating either angle *CBF*=54<sup>o </sup>or angle *BFE*=54<sup>o</sup>
> 
> **M1**: Awarded for correct method to calculate angle $x$ and is still awarded if using previously incorrect values in correct method [e.g. 180-('39'+'54')].
> 
> **A1**: For $x$ correctly evaluated as 87<sup>o </sup>and at least one correct reason used and stated.
> 
> **A1**: For $x$ correctly evaluated as 87<sup>o</sup> and full correct reasons stated for your method used.

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows two triangles $ABE$ and $ECD$

![Triangle diagram with angles labeled: angle A is x degrees, angle D is 42 degrees, and angle at point B is 296 degrees. Note: Diagram not accurately drawn.](assets/003-triangle-diagram-with-angles-labeled-angle-a-is-.png)

Triangle $ABE$ is isosceles with $AE=EB$
$ADE$ and $EBC$ are straight lines.

Angle $CDE=42^{\circ}$
The reflex angle $ECD=296^{\circ}$
 Angle $BAE=x^{\circ}$

Work out the value of $x$
parts.solution_md:
> *Angles around a point sum to 360*

$ECD=360-296=64^{\circ}$

**[M1]**

> *Angles in a triangle sum to 180*

$CED=180-42-64=74^{\circ}$

**[M1]**

> *Angles on a straight line sum to 180*

$AEB=180-74=106^{\circ}$

> *Base angles in an isosceles triangle are equal*

`x space equals space open parentheses 180 space minus space 106 close parentheses space divided by space 2`

**[M1]**

$x=37^{\circ}$

**[A1]**
